subject: Pilot plan: LexiMed trial — success criteria & model shortlist
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa@leximed.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Pilot plan: LexiMed trial — success criteria & model shortlist

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and an initial POC playbook so we can lock scope and owners. I put Aditya (AE) and Ben (Solutions Eng) on CC to own contract and technical delivery respectively.

Call recap (2 min):
- Goal: prove LexiMed clinical-assistant prototype can meet accuracy and latency targets across English + Spanish content and handle structured QA extractions from notes.
- Primary constraint: patient PHI stays in your VPC for the trial (you mentioned an on-prem connector).
- Success target: precision/recall for named-entity extraction >= 0.88 (combined), hallucination incidents <= 3 per 1k responses, 95th pct latency < 350ms for 512-token prompts.

Recommended POC scope (3 weeks):
1) Week 0 (kickoff, prep): ingestion of 20k sample snippets, test harness access, privacy/SOC checklist exchange.
2) Week 1 (baseline): run two model candidates on 1k holdout set, collect latency & quality baselines, confirm data residency setup.
3) Week 2 (tuning & regressions): apply prompt/system templates and small instruction-tuning via retrieval-augmented prompts, run evaluation matrix.
4) Week 3 (stress & rollout test): simulate concurrent calls (burst to 50 RPS), test fallback behavior, final readout & next-step decision.

Model shortlist (initial):
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized, low-latency path) — good English+limited Spanish, strong instruction following.
- Secondary: Llama-2-13B Q4 quantized variant — higher output fidelity for complex extractions; used as fallback when precision is prioritized.
- Fallback hosted variant: Redwood-rlhf-3b (hosted, higher safety, slower) — automatic route for safety-critical prompts or when we see hallucination spikes.

Multilingual notes: we will run a small Spanish validation set in Week 1. If Spanish recall < 0.82, plan to include an additional localized prompt template + small lexicon augmentation.

Evaluation rubric (attached): overall exact-match for extraction, entity-level F1, hallucination counts (manual spot checks), latency percentiles, and cost per 1k tokens. I attached the SOW draft and the evaluation spreadsheet (poc-eval-rubric.xlsx).

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Alyssa: confirm sample dataset share (SFTP or Drive) and confirm PHI routing requirement (VPC connector ok?).
- Ben: confirm we can provision a private model route in the LexiMed VPC and estimate expected 95th pct latency for Mistral-7B quantized.
- Aditya: I’ll put a short SOW together — please review commercial terms / trial credits.

Proposed kickoff: Monday 2026-06-22, 10am ET (30m). If that works we’ll send calendar invite and access checklist.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

redwood.com

From: Alyssa Green <alyssa@leximed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:09:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pilot plan: LexiMed trial — success criteria & model shortlist

Thanks Mina — that recap is useful. A few clarifications before we lock the kickoff: 

1) PHI / data path: we can share an SFTP or put files in our secure GDrive. For the trial we need the inference calls to route through our VPC (we have a private peering solution). Ben, does Redwood have experience with the VPC connector approach?
2) Latency: our internal target is 95th < 300ms for simple lookups; for long extraction tasks we can accept up to 450ms. Can you call out the expected profile for the two model choices?
3) Multilingual: Spanish is priority; Portuguese is lower but would be great to test if easy. I attached a small sample set (leximed-sample-clinical-snippets.csv) — please confirm confidentiality receipt.
4) Fallback behavior: curious how Redwood will route to the fallback model when tokens exceed a threshold or when hallucination guardrails trigger. Can we see a fallback demo in Week 3?

If Monday 6/22 10am ET works, we’ll do that. Also please include a short non-prod SLA in the SOW re: uptime for the duration of the POC.

Best — Alyssa
VP Product, LexiMed
alyssa@leximed.com

Attachment: leximed-sample-clinical-snippets.csv
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa@leximed.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pilot plan: LexiMed trial — success criteria & model shortlist

Thanks Alyssa — confirmed on receipt of the sample CSV and the confidentiality note. Quick answers and updated plan below.

PHI / VPC: Redwood supports private peering for trials. Ben will validate connector steps but we typically push only inference traffic through the customer VPC; logs/telemetry can be kept on customer side per the SOC checklist. We’ll send the VPC handshake doc ahead of kickoff.

Latency expectations (95th pct, 512-token prompt):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized): ~220-320ms (expected ~260ms for typical prompts)
- Llama-2-13B (Q4 quant): ~380-520ms (higher variability under burst)
- Redwood-rlhf-3b (hosted fallback): ~420-650ms

Given your 300ms target for simple lookups, we’ll route those to the Mistral-7B path and reserve Llama-13B for high-precision extraction flows (A/B configurable).

Fallback behavior we propose:
- Token-threshold trigger: if prompt+expected completion > 6k tokens, route to quantized Llama-13B (better context handling) or to hosted fallback if we detect safety flags.
- Hallucination guardrail: we’ll enable a detection rule (ensemble confidence + heuristic checks). If hallucination score > threshold for a request type, that request will be routed to Redwood-rlhf-3b and a signal logged to your Eval dashboard. Week 3 demo will include a synthetic hallucination trigger and show automatic reroute + notification.

Updated attachments: I attached an updated SOW (redwood-leximed-poc-sow.pdf) with non-prod SLA language, trial credits, and a checklist for VPC setup. The eval rubric (poc-eval-rubric.xlsx) already lists the metrics we’ll report weekly.

Proposed kickoff confirmed: Mon 2026-06-22, 10:00 ET. I’ll send the calendar invite and the VPC handshake doc. Ben — can you confirm provisioning ETA for an in-VPC Mistral route (rough estimate is fine)? Aditya — I’ll send the SOW for pricing/credits review after this note.

Thanks — Mina
